key_insight: Electrical current signals from the CNC spindle can reveal groove defects in friction stir welding before visible surface damage appears.
engineering_relevance: This enables low-cost, in-line monitoring of FSW using signals already available on industrial CNC machines, reducing the need for extra sensors.
method: Segment spindle and axis current signals during welding
Apply FFT, PSD, and spectral coherence analysis
Compare defect-free, defective, and transient groove-forming weld regions
evidence_signal: Defect-free regions showed high coherence, while defective regions showed reduced coherence at the spindle fundamental frequency and harmonics, with XCT confirming subsurface discontinuities and detection about 10 s after defect initiation.
watch_item: Performance was demonstrated on a specific dissimilar AA2139/AA7075 lap-joint case, so broader validation across materials, tools, and process settings is still needed.
paper_title: Early detection of groove defect in friction stir welding through data-driven process monitoring
